statements.status_notes: Debian tiff 4.7.0-3+deb13u3 ships the upstream PixarLog ABGR bounds fix as pixarlog-error-out-on-invalid-ABGR-output-buffer-siz.patch. The DHI package is rebuilt from that Debian source and keeps the fix.

The DHI tiff package backports upstream commit 6ba36f159fd396ad11bf6b7874554197736ecc8b from merge request 746, checking TIFFTAG_TILEBYTECOUNTS and TIFFTAG_STRIPBYTECOUNTS reads in tiff2ps before dereferencing the bytecount pointer.
The DHI tiff package backports upstream commit e8de4dc1f923576dce9d625caeebd93f9db697e1 from the v4.7.1rc1 release train, guarding thumbnail's computed colormap index before use.

The DHI tiff package backports the effective upstream tiffmedian/tiffdither fixes from commits ce46f002eca4148497363f80fab33f9396bcbeda and 78397815cdf7e9ad79943e00c3f06a6df9bf45c5. The intermediate conflict-resolution commit ecc4ddbf1f0fed7957d1e20361e37f01907898e0 is represented by the final upstream row-bound hunk.

This is an out-of-memory denial-of-service issue in TIFFReadEncodedStrip(). Debian treats it as unimportant with negligible security impact when applications follow the documented memory-allocation guidance, including TIFFOpenOptionsSetMaxSingleMemAlloc(). There is no upstream fix available to backport.
This is a tiff2ps CLI crash with no practical security impact for the DHI package. Debian marks the issue as minor/no-dsa, and there is no upstream fix available to backport.

This is a tiff2pdf crash through ijg-libjpeg behavior rather than a libtiff library flaw, and the Debian security tracker treats it as unimportant. The DHI package does not expose this CLI crash as a security boundary.

The original report has not been confirmed by the reporter after repeated attempts, third parties reported being unable to reproduce it, and SUSE analysis indicates the report is likely a duplicate of CVE-2017-9935. The DHI package treats this as a non-issue unless a reproducible upstream report becomes available.

The related upstream fix, commit 25f9ffa56548c1846c4a1f19308b7f561f7b1ab0, was included upstream before libtiff 4.0.9 and is present in the 4.7.0 Debian source used by the DHI package. The remaining memory-based denial-of-service behavior is not planned for a complete upstream fix and is not treated as a security-impacting issue for this package.

Debian tiff 4.7.0-3+deb13u2 already carries the upstream issue #721 fix corresponding to commit 0ac97aa7a5bffddd88f7cdbe517264e9db3f5bd5, including the tiffcrop tile buffer frees and the read_buff/crop_buff double-free guard. The DHI package is rebuilt from that Debian source and keeps the fix.
The DHI tiff package backports upstream commit 88cf9dbb48f6e172629795ecffae35d5052f68aa from the v4.7.1rc1 release train, bounding the tiffcrop sample dump loop by MAX_SAMPLES.

The DHI tiff package backports upstream commit 4d28af5fe61b1760f10981f5072ff1e6fd44f210 from the v4.7.1rc1 release train, which guards the tiffcrop null dereference path and validates tiffdither image width against the scanline size before use.
Marked no-dsa by Debian Security Team; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-36849
